chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Mu'amar ibn Khallad, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
Al-Nard (backgammon) and Al-Shatranj (chess) and Al-Arba'ata 'Ashara (a dice game) are in one status, and everything upon which gambling is played, it is Maysir (gambling).

key_terms.الشِّطْرَنْجُ: Shatranj, the ancient precursor to chess
key_terms.النَّرْدُ: Nard, an ancient dice game similar to backgammon
key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ: Al-Arba'ata 'Ashara, a specific dice game played with fourteen pieces
key_terms.مَيْسِرٌ: Maysir, a term for gambling or betting on games of chance

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on chess and backgammon according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise ruling from Imam al-Rida (AS), equating Nard (backgammon), Shatranj (chess), and Al-Arba'ata 'Ashara in their legal status. The Imam extends the prohibition to all games involving stakes, categorizing them under Maysir (gambling), a principle that has been central to Shia jurisprudence regarding leisure and wealth. This hadith serves as a primary textual basis for distinguishing between mere play and the prohibited element of wagering in recreational activities.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Moamar Bin Khallad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The dice and the chess, and the fourteen (a game) are at one status, and everything what is speculated upon, so it is gambling’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Mu’ammar ibn Khallad who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Dice, chess and checkers are all the same. Whatever is used in gambling (speculating) is gambling.”’
